task_specification.objective: Implement one bounded contract-hardening increment that makes dense profiling directly host-qualifiable while delivering the required authored upgrade-choice hierarchy and authored-cemetery spatial integrity.

diagnosis.root_cause: The dense profile is reachable but native frame-time qualification remains unavailable because the candidate does not yet provide a complete host-recapturable renderer-gated, reset-isolated three-cycle evidence contract.

stop_conditions: Do not replace, split, hide, duplicate, or surgically modify the preserved authored cemetery package or retained audio assets.
Do not assign deferred issue ids or expand into unrelated backlog gaps.
Candidate work stops at implementation and focused self-validation; GameLoop Runtime and Tester own runtime recapture and formal verdicts.

strategy.rationale: Repair the evidence boundary and player-facing contracts directly: strengthen dense setup/sample/reset provenance, replace text-stacked choices with authoritative visual cards, and reconcile the intact authored world with explicit camera, collision, landmark, and perimeter contracts instead of repeating transform-only tuning.

code: Run existing project script/resource parse and static checks on modified GDScript, scenes, resources, and project settings.
Verify tester_dense_* actions are editor/test-only guarded, cannot mutate release input maps, and preserve ordinary run balance when disabled.
Exercise valid, unavailable, newly unlocked, malformed, duplicate, and unchanged upgrade offers to verify safe normalization and delta filtering.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime and Tester recapture boot, ordinary gameplay, upgrade draft with mouse/keyboard/gamepad focus, cemetery spawn, central-landmark approach/near-contact/departure, cardinal views, perimeter movement replay, and dense prepare/advance/reset.

Capture runtime_state, scene/spatial bounds, collision and visibility receipts, screenshots, and three complete 1920x1080 dense cycles with frame-time distributions, high-water marks, lifecycle deltas, renderer classification, and reset-isolation receipts.
Re-run host_godot_boot and native_godot_project preservation checks; Tester determines whether the dense gate and required capabilities pass.
visual: Inspect replacement upgrade cards over the gameplay/pause backdrop for authored silhouettes/icons, compact changed stats, truthful current-to-new values, no NEW/LOCKED CURRENT placeholders, restrained copy, and distinct keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states.

Compare spawn, landmark, cardinal, perimeter, and dense screenshots for larger traversable scale, external depth, central landmark readability, warm/cool nocturnal hierarchy, stable collision-aligned visibility, no disappearance/occlusion drift, no abrupt void, and no visible primitive stand-ins.

done_when: Editor-only tester_dense_prepare, tester_dense_advance, and tester_dense_reset actions leave stable inspectable states, expose requested/resolved/reset-isolation receipts plus branch, setup-generation, cycle, and run identity, and are unavailable in release exports.

At 1920x1080 and 25-40 enemies, the dense profile records nonzero frame, physics, and render samples with bounded distributions and high-water marks for enemies, projectiles, pickups, effects, lights, UI, and audio; three complete reset-isolated cycles are comparable and renderer qualification is deferred until native hardware evidence.

Text-stacked weapon and upgrade choices are replaced by an authored visual hierarchy: every card leads with a weapon or upgrade silhouette/icon, uses compact stat icons, shows truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant changed stat deltas, omits unchanged or exhaustive rows, never uses NEW or LOCKED as a CURRENT value, and provides complete keyboard, mouse, and game​?

The authored cemetery provides larger traversable scale, a coherent external world with external depth beyond the playable boundary, and a readable central building/landmark without replacing the intact package.

Visible geometry and collision agree around the landmark and every boundary/perimeter; ordinary movement and movement replay around each landmark side cannot pass through, trigger disappearance, or produce camera occlusion that hides the player or landmark.
Spawn, cardinal, landmark, perimeter, and dense runtime captures preserve a recoverable escape lane, stable visibility, and no abrupt empty void or proxy-floor presentation.
tasks.instructions: Implement a single bounded release-convergence pass across dense qualification, upgrade presentation, and authored cemetery spatial integrity. Preserve authoritative gameplay state and the intact authored environment. Harden the existing dense profile and RunController instrumentation so tester_dense_prepare/advance/reset are isolated, release-guarded, deterministic, and emit complete requested/resolved/reset-isolation, renderer, viewport, cycle, and sample receipts without changing ordinary gameplay balance. Replace text-stacked weapon and upgrade choices with an authored visual hierarchy: lead with recognizable weapon or upgrade silhouettes, use compact stat icons, show truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, omit unchanged or exhaustive rows, never place NEW or LOCKED in the CURRENT column, keep copy restrained, and provide complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states. Reconcile camera framing, outer datum, native landmark collision, spawn/navigation exclusion, and perimeter visibility in one transform-space contract; expand to larger traversable scale where required, retain external world/external depth, keep the central building/landmark visible, and verify collision, disappearance/occlusion, boundary/perimeter, and ordinary movement/movement replay behavior. Do not add generated roads, floor patches, facade slices, duplicate landmarks, replacement asset families, or decorative proxy clutter.
